newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Guangdong tightens watch on futures firms.
newsitem.headline: China's Guangdong tightens watch on futures firms.

text.p: Southern China's Guangdong Securities Regulatory Commission has launched a crackdown on local futures firms as part of a nationwide bid to tighten control, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Wednesday.
The move was a response to a series of recent policies from Beijing aimed at tightening control of China's fledgling commodities futures market, the newspaper said.

The Guangdong commission had told local futures brokerages to submit quarterly and annual reports on their operations, and ordered brokerages set up without the approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) to halt business immediately, the newspaper said.

The CSRC, China's top securities watchdog, earlier this week announced it had decided to assign supervisors to all futures exchanges to monitor their operations. The supervisors would be based in the exchanges to monitor their daily operations and financial situation and would make regular reports to the CSRC.
The Guangdong commission has also drafted detailed rules designed to counter speculation on the province's futures markets, the newspaper said.
Futures trading agencies violating the regulation face business suspension or compulsory closure, it said without giving details.
Earlier this month, the Guangdong commission's counterpart in the neighbouring southern island province of Hainan drafted similar policies to rein in local futures trading.

The Hainan regulatory authority had said it would launch an annual inspection of the financial circumstances, operations and risk controls of local futures brokerages. Those found with poor results would be closed, it said.

It said Hainan would accelerate the closure of unlicensed brokerages to clean up the market. Financial institutions that had holdings in futures brokerages must transfer all their stakes to non-financial ventures.
